title: I'm making a game that transforms any Wikipedia page into a FPS level - WikiFPS
author: I_Only_Like_Giraffes
selftext:
A year and a half ago, I had the idea to make a game that could transform any Wikipedia page into a custom FPS level. As a further challenge, I decided to exclusively use art assets from Wikimedia Commons - including every image, texture, sound effect and even the music. As you can imagine, it was often tricky to find assets that worked well. Thankfully, a padlock closing makes a pretty good reload sound.

I used codex to build a custom engine for the game. It designs each level based on the unique elements of each page like length and paragraph count. Each section of the article becomes a new room with all of the page's text included in the walls. That means you can actually read the full article while playing through a level.

Each image from the page is transformed into different enemy types. Players must find a key within the level to unlock a boss room, then defeat the boss to finish the level. You can pick any Wikipedia article to continue down the rabbit hole. Defeat all 13 Million+ levels to win! (yes, this includes the page on penises)

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: What would be sick is being able to pull assets from other wiki pages on the fly. For example, if you're fighting the Napoleon wiki page, you could quickly use the search bar to pull up something completely unrelated, like an M1 Abrams tank. Next thing you know, you're facing Napoleon with a freaking tank.
